problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-\frac{17}{4}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the change of variables given by the matrix equation

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

and the curve $C,$ defined as

$$
C:\,2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=-26.
$$

 

Given that the change of variables above reduces $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}$ to its canonical (diagonal) form $6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2},$ what type of a quadratic curve is defined by $C?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,{{2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=-26
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2} & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2})-2\sqrt{5}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2}) & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2} & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2} & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+({y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2}+25)-25 & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{({y}_{2}-5)}^{2}-25 & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{({y}_{2}-5)}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables

$$
{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1}={y}_{1}, \\ {z}_{2}={y}_{2}-5,\end{aligned}
$$

 

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{z}_{1}^{2}+{z}_{2}^{2} & =-1 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}})^{2}}+{z}_{2}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

This defines an empty set, also called an imaginary ellipse. Notice that the left-hand side is non-negative for all ${z}_{1}$ and ${z}_{2},$ while the right-hand side is negative.
